Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)

Surat al-Anbiya' (The Prophets)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near for them﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surat an-Nahl, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here.

Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, mentions in this noble verse that the disbelievers concealed their secret counsel among themselves, saying: the Prophet ﷺ is only a human being like yourselves, so how could he be a messenger to them? The *najwa* (secret counsel) is speaking covertly and concealing it from people.

What this noble verse indicates is their claim that a human like themselves cannot be a messenger, and Allah's refutation of them in this matter has come in many verses, some of which we have already mentioned,

• such as His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [Al-Isra: 94]

• and His saying: ﴿So they said, "Shall human beings guide us?" And they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need﴾, to the end of the verse [At-Taghabun: 6]

• and His saying: ﴿"Shall we follow a single human from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness"﴾ [Al-Qamar: 24]

• and His saying: ﴿"This is none but a human like you. He eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink. And if you obey a human like yourselves, indeed you would then be losers"﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 33–34]

• and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"What is with this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?"﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-Furqan: 7]

• and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "You are but human beings like us, who want to avert us from what our fathers used to worship"﴾, to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 10].

The verses of this kind are very numerous, as the clarification of that has already preceded.

Allah has also refuted this false claim, namely the prevention of human beings from being sent,

• such as His saying here in this noble surah: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 7],

• and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you and given them wives and descendants﴾, to the end of the verse [Ar-Ra'd: 38]

• and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [Al-Furqan: 20]. His saying here: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 8], and other verses besides these.

The clause ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ has been said to be a *badal* (substitution, apposition) of *al-najwa*, i.e., they concealed the secret counsel which is this covert speech, which is their saying: "Is this not but a human like you?" Az-Zamakhshari began with this view. It has also been said that it is an object (*maf'ul bihi*) of *al-najwa*, because it carries the meaning of covert speech, i.e., they said secretly: ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾. It has also been said that it is the object of a deleted verb of saying, i.e., they said: "Is this not but a human like you?" and this is the most apparent of these views, because the deletion of the verb of saying with its content remaining is common (*ittirad*).

As for His saying ﴿those who did wrong﴾, there are many well-known grammatical possibilities (*i'rab*), and the most apparent of them in my view is that it is a *badal* of the *waw* in His saying ﴿and they concealed﴾, a *badal al-ba'd min al-kull* (substitution of part for whole). It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence (*al-usul*) that the substitution of part for whole is among the connected specifiers (*al-mukhassisat al-muttasilah*),

• such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for Allah is the duty of pilgrimage to the House upon the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 97].

So His saying *man* (whoever) is a *badal* of *an-nas* (the people): a substitution of part for whole, and it specifies the obligation of Hajj by stating that it is obligatory only upon those who are able to find a way to it. We have already mentioned this in Surah Al-Ma'idah.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾

The grammatical analysis of this clause follows the analysis of the clause before it, which is ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾. The meaning is that they claimed that what our Prophet ﷺ brought was magic, and based on that false claim, they denounced themselves for approaching magic while they could see. By this they meant rejecting the Prophet's ﷺ truthfulness, i.e., "We cannot accept you and follow you, while we see that what you have brought is magic." Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, has clarified in another place that they claimed that what he ﷺ brought was magic,

• such as His saying concerning some of them: ﴿This is nothing but magic that is transmitted﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 24],

• and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "A magician or a madman"﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 52]. Allah has refuted their claim that the Qur'an is magic

• by His saying here: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows the word in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 4], meaning that the One who knows the word in the heavens and the earth, who is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, whose knowledge encompasses everything, is the One who sent down this great Qur'an. The fact that the One who sent it down is the Knower of everything indicates the perfection of its truthfulness in its reports, its justice in its rulings, and its freedom from all defects and deficiencies, and that it is not magic. This meaning has been clarified in another place,

• such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say, "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth"﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-Furqan: 6]

• and His saying, Exalted is He: (p-135) ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [An-Nisa': 166]

and other verses besides these. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim recited this letter ﴿Qala Rabbi ya'lamu al-qawl﴾ with an *alif* after the *qaf* and a *fatha* on the *lam*, in the form of the past-tense verb. The rest recited *Qul* with a *damma* on the *qaf* and a *sukun* on the *lam*, in the imperative form.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 5:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿بَلْ قالُوا أضْغاثُ أحْلامٍ بَلِ افْتَراهُ بَلْ هو شاعِرٌ﴾ .

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, they say: "A confusion of dreams." Nay, he has invented it. Nay, he is a poet.﴾

The apparent meaning is that the "bal" (nay) in His saying here, ﴿Nay, they say: "A confusion of dreams"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 5], etc., is a transitional *idrab* (a change of subject, marking a move from one claim to another), not a nullifying *idrab* (one that retracts the previous claim), because they said all of that. Some scholars said:

All these differing claims that Allah related about them came from a single group that did not hold firm to one position. Rather, at one time they say he is a sorcerer, at another a poet, and so on, because the one who speaks falsely does not stick to one statement. Other scholars of knowledge said: each one of those claims was made by a separate group, as we previously pointed out in surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, ﴿Those who have made the Qur'an into fragments﴾ [al-Hijr: 91]. Allah has refuted these false assertions in verses of His Book, such as His refutation of their claim that he is a poet or a soothsayer, in His saying: ﴿It is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you reflect. It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had invented about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have severed from him the aorta, and not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41–47].

And His saying: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an, to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69–70].

And His saying in refuting their claim that he invented it: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been invented apart from Allah, but it is a confirmation of what came before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds. Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ [Yunus: 37–38].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ [Hud: 13].

And His saying: ﴿It is not a narration that is invented, but a confirmation of what is before it and a detailing of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Yusuf: 111], and other verses besides these.

And like His saying in refuting their claim that he is a soothsayer or a madman: ﴿So you, by the blessing of your Lord, are neither a soothsayer nor a madman﴾ [al-Tur: 29].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your companion is not mad﴾ [al-Takwir: 22].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "I exhort you to one thing: that you stand before Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment"﴾ (p-136) [Saba': 46].

And His saying: ﴿Or they did not recognize their Messenger, so they deny him? Or do they say, "There is madness in him"? Nay, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 69–70, cf. 23], and other verses clarifying the nullity of everything they claimed about the Prophet ﷺ and the Qur'an.

His saying ﴿A confusion of dreams﴾ [al-Anbiya: 5] means: mixtures, like the varied dreams that a sleeper sees, which have no reality behind them, as the poet said:

"The tales of Tasm and Jadis, or a mirage in a wide plain, shimmering for the traveller at night, or the jumbled dreams of one who dreams."

And from al-Yazidi: *adghath* (confusions) are those things which have no interpretation.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let him bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers proposed to our Prophet that he should bring them a sign like the signs of the messengers before him: such as the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa, the wind of Sulayman, the raising of the dead by 'Isa, his healing of the blind and the leper, and the like. The explanation of the point of comparison in His saying ﴿as the earlier ones were sent﴾ is that it means: "as the earlier ones brought signs," because the sending of messengers necessarily includes bringing signs. So your saying "He sent Muhammad ﷺ with a miracle" [is equivalent]. Allah has made clear that the signs they proposed, had they come to them, would not have led them to faith, and that if they had come and they persisted in their disbelief, Allah would have destroyed them with a total punishment, as He destroyed the people of Salih when they hamstrung the she-camel. Like His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier ones denied them. We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her with it﴾ [al-Isra': 59], the verse in full; and like His saying: ﴿They swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe in it. Say: "Signs are only with Allah." And what would make you aware that when they come they will not believe?﴾ [al-An'am: 109]. He pointed to this here in His saying: ﴿No town that We destroyed believed before them. Will they then believe?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 6], meaning that the nations who proposed signs before them, and whose messengers brought them what they proposed, did not believe, but persisted, so Allah destroyed them. You are even more stubborn and obstinate than they were. So if what you proposed came to you, you would not believe, and you would perish as they perished. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them﴾ [Yunus: 96–97], and other verses besides these.

He also made clear that a sign that is greater than all signs did come to them, so whoever is not satisfied with it deserves rebuke and reproach. This is in His saying: ﴿They say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "Signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed, in it is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 50–51]. We have already mentioned that this meaning is indicated by His saying: ﴿They say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ (p-137) [Ta-Ha: 133], and by His saying: ﴿We did not send before you except men﴾ up to His saying ﴿nor were they immortal﴾ [al-Anbiya: 7–8]. We have already presented the verses that clarify this, so repeating it here is unnecessary.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

In these verses, may He be glorified and exalted, He made clear that He sent the Messengers to the nations and they denied them, and that He promised the Messengers that they would have victory and the good outcome, and that He fulfilled that promise to His Messengers and saved them. And He saved with them whom He willed to save. What is meant by this is those among their nations who believed in them, and He destroyed the transgressors, namely the disbelievers who denied the Messengers. This meaning has been clarified in many places in His Book,

such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when the Messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and whom We willed was saved. And Our punishment is not averted from the guilty people.﴾ [Yusuf: 110]

And His saying: ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise to His Messengers. Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution.﴾ [Ibrahim: 47]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿"And We will surely make you inhabit the land after them."﴾ [Ibrahim: 13-14]

And His saying: ﴿And My word has already preceded for My servants, the messengers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they would be the ones given victory.﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ [As-Saffat: 171-173]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us,﴾ the verse [Hud: 58]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us,﴾ the verse [Hud: 66]

And His saying: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us,﴾ [Hud: 94], and other verses besides these. The apparent meaning is that "ṣadaqa" is transitive both directly and with a preposition. You say: "ṣadaqtuhu al-wa'd" (I fulfilled to him the promise), and "ṣadaqtuhu fi al-wa'd" (I was truthful to him regarding the promise),

such as His saying here: ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 9]

And His saying: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152]

So the saying of az-Zamakhshari, "﴿We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men﴾" – there is no need for this, and Allah knows best. And "al-israf" (excess) is exceeding the limit in acts of disobedience such as disbelief, and for this reason the term "al-musrifun" is frequently applied to the disbelievers in the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and raised up after it another people.﴾

"Kam" (how many) here is used to indicate a large number, and it is in the accusative position, because it is the object of "qasamna" (We shattered). The meaning is: We shattered many of the towns that had been wrongdoing, and We raised up after them another people. This meaning mentioned here is explained in many places in the Book of Allah.

- Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How many generations did We destroy after Noah. And sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants.﴾ [al-Isra: 17]

- And His saying: ﴿How many a town We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so it lies fallen upon its roofs.﴾ and the verse [al-Hajj: 45]

- And His saying: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to account with severe accounting and punished it with a terrible punishment.﴾ ﴿So it tasted the evil of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.﴾ [al-Talaq: 8-9]

and other verses besides these.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿How many a town did We shatter﴾. The original meaning of "qasm" (shattering) is the most grievous kind of breaking, because it is the breaking that separates the parts so that they no longer fit together, unlike "fasm" (with the letter fa'), which is a breaking that does not entirely sever the fitting together of the parts. What is meant by "qasm" in the verse is severe destruction.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Hijr" (Surah 15), so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. Likewise His saying: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 18], the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il" (Surah 17). Likewise the verses that follow this one: we have already presented in many places what clarifies them from the Book of Allah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 26:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.﴾ ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers, may Allah curse them, said about Him that He has taken a son. We have already explained this thoroughly on previous occasions in several places of this blessed Book. Exalted is He far above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation. Here He demonstrates the falsehood of what they claimed about their Lord regarding the taking of children, namely the angels in their assumption, by the particle of retraction (idrab) that is "bal" (rather), which negates the claim, clarifying that they are His honored servants, and a servant cannot be a son of his master. Then He praised His angels, that they are honored servants who do not precede their Lord in speech, that is, they do not say except what He commands them to say, because of the intensity of their obedience to Him: ﴿and they act by His command.﴾ What He indicated in this noble verse, that the angels are His servants and His property, and that a servant cannot be a son of his master, He indicated elsewhere, such as His saying in "al-Baqarah": ﴿And they say, "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116], and His saying in "an-Nisa'": ﴿Allah is but one God. Glory be to Him above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [an-Nisa': 171], that is: the one who owns everything cannot have a son, because ownership contradicts sonship, and there cannot exist anything other than Him except that it is His possession, exalted is He. (p-139)

What He mentioned in this noble verse of the good praise of His angels, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, He clarified in other places:

• Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and strong, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.﴾ [at-Tahrim: 6]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, there are over you guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do.﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belong whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire. They exalt Him night and day; they never slacken.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19-20]

And other verses besides these.

Issue

Some scholars derived from this noble verse and its like in the Qur'an that if a father comes to own his son, the son becomes free upon him by that ownership. The basis of this is clear: the disbelievers claimed that the angels are daughters of Allah. So Allah negated that claim by stating that they are His servants and His property, and this indicates that ownership is incompatible with sonship, and that the two cannot validly coexist. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾

The pronoun in His saying "among them" refers to the angels mentioned in His saying: ﴿But they are servants honored﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26]. The meaning is that they, despite their honor with Allah, if any one of them claimed that he had the right to direct some of Allah's exclusive rights toward himself, he would be a polytheist (mushrik), and his recompense would be Hell. It is known that conditional statement (ta'liq) is valid regarding what is impossible and does not occur, such as His saying: ﴿Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 81], and His saying: ﴿If there were in them (the heavens and earth) gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22]. The purpose of this is to magnify the matter of shirk (association of partners with Allah). This supposition and hypothetical assumption which He, exalted is He, mentioned here concerning the angels, He also mentioned concerning the messengers, upon all of them be the blessings and peace of Allah. He, exalted, said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ [az-Zumar: 65]. When He, exalted is He, mentioned those prophets mentioned in Surat al-An'am in His saying: ﴿And of his descendants, David﴾ [al-An'am: 84], up to the end of those He mentioned, He said after that: ﴿That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been nullified for them﴾ [al-An'am: 88].

(p-140) His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell﴾ (to the end of the verse) [al-Anbiya': 29] is a definitive proof that the rights of Allah which are purely His, from all types of worship, may not be directed toward anyone, even an honored angel or a sent prophet. Among what clarifies this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture and judgment and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah." But [he would say], "Be learned religious scholars (rabbaniyyin) by what you have been teaching of the Scripture and by what you have been studying." And He would not order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 79-80]. And His saying, may He be exalted, addressing the master of creation, blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah." But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 64].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them and made⁠﴾.

Most of the seven readers, except Ibn Kathir, recited this letter as "Awa lam yara" with a waw after the hamza. Ibn Kathir recited it as "Alam yara alladhina kafaru" without the waw, and it is so written in the Mushaf of Makkah. The interrogation is a rebuke and reproach of the disbelievers, since they witness the wondrous artistry and marvels of Allah, yet still worship besides Him that which neither benefits its worshipper, nor harms those who disobey it, nor has power over anything.

As for His saying "kanatā" (were), the dual refers to the two kinds, the kind of heaven and the kind of earth, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease⁠﴾ [Fatir: 41]. A parallel to this is the saying of Umar ibn Shayba:

"Does it not grieve you that the mountains of Qays and Taghlib have separated in severance?"

Al-Ratq (the joining, sealing) is the verbal noun of "rataqahu ratqan," meaning he sealed it. From it comes "al-ratqa'" (the woman whose vagina is closed). The verbal noun is used here as a description, which is why it is singular and He did not say "ratqayn" (two joined masses). Al-Fatq (the parting) is the separation between two things that were joined; it is the opposite of al-ratq. From it is the poet's saying:

"It is easy for them when they become angry, the anger of enemies and their humiliation,
and the sealing of rifts and the parting of tightened bonds, and the undoing of matters and their tightening."

Know that the scholars differed over the meaning of ratq and fatq in this verse, in five opinions. Some of them are utterly weak, and one of them is supported by indications from the Glorious Qur'an:

(p-141) The first: the meaning of ﴿were a joined mass⁠﴾ is that the heavens and the earth were adhering to one another, then Allah parted them and separated the heavens from the earth, raising the heaven to its place, settling the earth in its place, and separating them by the air that is between them, as you see.

The second opinion: the seven heavens were a joined mass, each adhering to the other, and Allah parted them and made them seven heavens, with a separation between every two of them. The earths likewise were a joined mass, and He parted them and made them seven, some separated from others.

The third opinion: the meaning of ﴿were a joined mass⁠﴾ is that the heaven did not send down rain, and the earth did not produce plants in it; then Allah parted the heaven with rain and the earth with vegetation.

The fourth opinion: ﴿were a joined mass⁠﴾ means they were in darkness, in which, due to its intensity, nothing could be seen; then Allah parted them with light. This opinion in reality returns to the first and second opinions.

The fifth: - and it is the most remote of them, for the weakness of it is evident - that ratq is intended to mean non-existence and fatq is intended to mean bringing into existence, i.e., they were non-existent and We brought them into existence. This opinion is as you see.

Having learned the opinions of the people of knowledge on this verse, know that the third of them - namely that they were a joined mass in the sense that the heaven did not send down rain and the earth did not produce anything, so Allah parted the heaven with rain and the earth with vegetation - has been indicated by evidences from the Book of Allah, exalted is He:

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have those who disbelieve not considered that⁠﴾ [21] indicates that they saw that; because the more apparent sense of "ra'a" (saw) is that it is visual, and what they see with their eyes is that the heaven sends down no rain and the earth is dead, dry, with no vegetation in it. So they witness with their eyes Allah sending down rain and bringing forth through it all kinds of plants.

The second indication: He followed that with His saying: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not believe?⁠﴾ [21]. The apparent connection of this statement is with what precedes it, i.e., and We made from the water that We sent down by Our parting of the heaven, and by which We brought forth all kinds of plants by Our parting of the earth, every living thing.

The third indication: this meaning has come clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿By the sky with its return⁠﴾ ﴿and the earth with its cracking⁠﴾ [al-Tariq: 11-12], because "al-raj'" (return) means the descent of rain from it time after time, and "al-sad'" (cracking) means the splitting of the earth to bring forth plants; and like His saying: ﴿Then let man look at his food: that We pour down water in torrents⁠﴾ ﴿then We split the earth in splits⁠﴾ (p-142) [Abasa: 24-26], and the verse continues.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Atiyya and others chose this opinion, because of the indications we have mentioned. What supports this is the frequent citation in the Glorious Qur'an of the descent of rain and the growth of plants as evidence for the perfection of Allah's power, the greatness of His favour upon His creation, and His power to resurrect. As for those who said that the meaning of ratq and fatq is that they were joined and Allah parted them and separated some from others, they said regarding His saying "Have they not seen that" that it is from "ra'a" in the sense of knowledge, not sight, and they said: the reasoning for their position is that it has come in the Qur'an, and what has come in the Qur'an is a definite matter with no room for doubt. And Allah knows best.

The closest of the opinions in this matter is what we have mentioned, the indication of the Qur'anic evidences for it. Imam al-Razi said in his tafsir: "They preferred this view over all others by His saying after it: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not⁠﴾, and that does not fit unless the water has a connection with what came before, and it is not so unless the meaning is what we have mentioned."

If it is said: this view is weak, because rain does not descend from the heavens but from one heaven, which is the lowest heaven.

We say: the plural was applied to it only because each piece of it is a heaven, as one says: "a thawb akhlaq" (a worn garment) and "burma a'shar" (a cooking pot in pieces). End of his words.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not believe?⁠﴾

The apparent meaning is that "ja'ala" (made) here means "khalaqa" (created), since it takes one object. This is supported by His saying in Surat al-Nur: ﴿And Allah created every creature from water⁠﴾ [al-Nur: 45].

The scholars differed over the meaning of creating every thing from water. Some scholars said: the water from which every thing was created is the sperm-drop (nutfa), because Allah created all animals that are born by way of reproduction from sperm-drops, and on this view it is a general term with a specific application.

Some scholars said: it is ordinary water, because animals are either created from it directly, like some animals that come into being from water, or indirectly, since the sperm-drops come from foods, and all foods arise from water. This is plain in grains, fruits and the like, and likewise in meats, milks, fats and the like, since all of it arises through water.

Some people of knowledge said: the meaning of His creating every animal from water is that it is as if He created it from water (p-143) because of its extreme need for it and its impatience without it, like His saying: ﴿Man was created of haste⁠﴾ [al-Anbiya: 37], and other opinions. We have already mentioned the four meanings in which the word "ja'ala" comes and what comes of it in the Qur'an and what does not come in it, in Surat al-Nahl.

Al-Razi said in his tafsir of this noble verse, and his words are: "One may say: how does He say, 'And We created from water every animal,' when He has said: ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind⁠﴾ [al-Hijr: 27], and it has come in reports that Allah created the angels from light, and He said regarding Isa, peace be upon him: ﴿And when you shape from clay like the form of a bird by My permission, then you breathe into it and it becomes a bird by My permission⁠﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 110], and He said regarding Adam: ﴿He created him from dust⁠﴾ [Ali Imran: 59]."

The answer: although the wording is general, the restricting indication is present, for the proof must be witnessed and perceptible, so that it is closer to the intended meaning. By this route the angels, the jinn, Adam, and the story of Isa, peace be upon them, are excluded, because the disbelievers did not see any of that. End of his words.

Then al-Razi also said: "The exegetes differed. Some of them said: by His saying ﴿every living thing⁠﴾ is meant only animals. Others said: rather, it includes plants and trees, since from water they became growing, and moisture, greenery, blossom and fruit came into them. This view is more fitting to the intended meaning, as if He, exalted is He, said: We parted the heaven to send down rain, and We made from it every thing on the earth, of plants and other things, living. The argument of the first view is that plants are not called living. We say: we do not concede that, and the proof for it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How He gives life to the earth after its death⁠﴾ [al-Rum: 50]." End of his words also.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with them, and We placed therein broad pathways as ways, that they might be guided.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Nahl" (Surah 16), so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا لِبَشَرٍ مِن قَبْلِكَ الخُلْدَ أفَإنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ المَوْتِ﴾.

قال بعض أهل العلم: كان المشركون ينكرون نبوته ﷺ ويقولون: هو شاعر يُتَرَبَّصُ به رَيْبُ المَنُونِ (أي تُنتظر به نوائب الدهر)، ولعله يموت كما مات شاعر بني فلان، فقال الله تعالى: ﴿قَدْ ماتَ﴾ (p-145) الأنبياءُ مِن قبلك، وتولّى دينَه بالنصر والحياطة، فهكذا نحفظ دينك وشرعك.

وقال بعض أهل العلم: لما نعى جبريل إلى النبي ﷺ نفسَه قال: "فمن لأمتي؟" فنزلت ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا لِبَشَرٍ مِن قَبْلِكَ الخُلْدَ﴾ [الأنبياء: 34]. والأول أظهر؛ لأن السورة مكية، ومعنى الآية أن الله لم يجعل لبشر قبل نبيه الخلدَ، أي دوامَ البقاء في الدنيا، بل كلهم يموت.

وقوله: ﴿أفَإنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ استفهامٌ إنكاريٌّ معناه النفي. والمعنى: أنك إن مِتَّ فهم لن يَخلدوا بعدك، بل سيموتون، ولذلك أتبعه بقوله: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ المَوْتِ﴾ [آل عمران: 185]. وما أشار إليه ـ جلّ وعلا ـ في هذه الآية من أنه ﷺ سيموت، وأنهم سيموتون، وأن الموت ستذوقه كل نفس، أوضحه في غير هذا الموضع،

• كقوله تعالى: ﴿إنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وإنَّهم مَيِّتُونَ﴾ [الزمر: 3]

• وكقوله: ﴿كُلُّ مَن عَلَيْها فانٍ﴾ ﴿وَيَبْقى وجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الجَلالِ والإكْرامِ﴾ [الطور: 26-27]

• وقوله في سورة "آل عمران": ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ المَوْتِ وإنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النّارِ وأُدْخِلَ الجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فازَ﴾ [آل عمران: 185]

• وقوله في سورة "العنكبوت": ﴿ياعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّ أرْضِي واسِعَةٌ فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ المَوْتِ ثُمَّ إلَيْنا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ [العنكبوت: 56-57]

• وقوله تعالى في سورة "النساء": ﴿أيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكُكُمُ المَوْتُ ولَوْ كُنْتُمْ في بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ﴾ [النساء: 78]

إلى غير ذلك من الآيات. وقد قدّمنا في سورة "الكهف" استدلالَ بعض أهل العلم بهذه الآية الكريمة على موت الخضر عليه السلام. وقال بعض أهل العلم في قوله: ﴿فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ إنه استفهامٌ حُذفت أداتُه، أي: أفَهُمُ الخالدون؟ وقد تقرر في علم النحو أن حذف همزة الاستفهام إذا دلّ المقامُ عليها جائزٌ، وهو قياسيٌّ عند الأخفش مع "أمْ"، ودونها ذِكرُ الجواب أم لا. فمن أمثلته دون "أم" ودون ذكر الجواب قولُ الكُمَيْت:

طَرِبْتُ وما شَوْقًا إلى البِيضِ أطْرَبُ ولا لَعِبًا مِنِّي وذُو الشَّيْبِ يَلْعَبُ

يعني: أوَذُو الشيب يلعب. وقولُ أبي خِراشٍ الهُذَلي واسمُه خُوَيْلِدٌ:

رَفَوْنِي وقالُوا يا خُوَيْلِدُ لَمْ تُرَعْ ∗∗∗ فَقُلْتُ وأنْكَرْتُ الوُجُوهَ هُمُ هُمُ

يعني: أهم هم على التحقيق. ومن أمثلته دون "أم" مع ذكر الجواب قولُ عمرَ بنِ أبي ربيعةَ المخزومي:

ثُمَّ قالُوا تُحِبُّها قُلْتُ بَهْرا ∗∗∗ عَدَدَ النَّجْمِ والحَصى والتُّرابِ

(p-146) يعني: أتحبها على الصحيح؟ وهو مع "أم" كثيرٌ جدًّا، وأنشد له سيبويهِ قولَ الأسودِ بنِ يَعْفُرَ التميمي:

لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدْرِي وإنْ كُنْتُ دارِيًا ∗∗∗ شُعَيْثُ بْنُ سَهْمٍ أمْ شُعَيْثُ بْنُ مِنقَرِ

يعني: أشُعيثُ بنُ سهمٍ؟ ومنه قولُ ابنِ أبي ربيعةَ المخزومي:

بَدا لِي مِنها مِعْصَمٌ يَوْمَ جَمَّرَتْ ∗∗∗ وكَفٌّ خَضِيبٌ زُيِّنَتْ بِبَنانِ
فَواللَّهِ ما أدْرِي وإنِّي لَحاسِبٌ ∗∗∗ بِسَبْعٍ رَمَيْتُ الجَمْرَ أمْ بِثَمانِ

يعني: أبسبعٍ؟ وقولُ الأخطل:

كِذَبَتْكَ عَيْنُكَ أمْ رَأيْتَ بِواسِطٍ ∗∗∗ غَلَسَ الظَّلامِ مِنَ الرَّبابِ خَيالًا

يعني: أكذبتْكَ عينُكَ؟ كما نصّ سيبويهِ في كتابه على جواز ذلك في بيت الأخطل هذا، وإن خالف في ذلك الخليلَ قائلًا: إن "كَذَبَتْكَ" صيغةٌ خبريةٌ ليس فيها استفهامٌ محذوف، وإن "أمْ" بمعنى "بَلْ". ففي البيت على قول الخليل نوعٌ من أنواع البديع المعنويّ يُسمّى "الرجوعَ". وقد أوضحنا هذه المسألة وأكثرنا من شواهدها العربية في كتابنا (دفعُ إيهامِ الاضطرابِ عن آياتِ الكتابِ) في سورة "آل عمران"، وذكرنا أن قولَه تعالى في آية "الأنبياء" هذه ﴿فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ من أمثلة ذلك، والعلمُ عند الله تعالى.

وقوله تعالى في هذه الآية الكريمة: ﴿أفَإنْ مِتَّ﴾ قرأه نافعٌ وحفصٌ عن عاصمٍ وحمزةُ والكسائيُّ "مِتَّ" بكسر الميم، والباقون بضم الميم، وقد أوضحنا في سورة "مريم" وجهَ كسرِ الميم. وقوله في هذه الآية الكريمة: ﴿أفَإنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ يُفهم منه أنه لا ينبغي للإنسان أن يفرح بموت أحدٍ لأجل أمرٍ دنيويٍّ ينالُه بسبب موته؛ لأنه هو ليس مخلَّدًا بعده.

وروي عن الشافعيّ أنه أنشد هذين البيتين مستشهدًا بهما:

تَمَنّى رِجالٌ أنْ أمُوتَ وإنْ أمُتْ ∗∗∗ فَتِلْكَ سَبِيلٌ لَسْتُ فِيها بِأوْحَدِ
فَقُلْ لِلَّذِي يَبْقى خِلافَ الَّذِي ∗∗∗ مَضى تَهَيَّأْ لِأُخْرى مِثْلِها فَكَأنْ قَدِ

ونظيرُ هذا قولُ الآخَر:

فَقُلْ لِلشّامِتِينَ بِنا أفِيقُوا ∗∗∗ سَيَلْقى الشّامِتُونَ كَما لَقِينا

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 35:

Allah's words: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial; and to Us you will be returned.﴾

(p-147) The meaning: We test you with what calls for patience among afflictions, and with what calls for gratitude among blessings. And to Us is your return, so We will recompense you according to what is found in you of patience or gratitude. As for His words "fitnah" (as a trial), it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing "wa-nabluwakum" without being derived from its own verb form.

What He, may He be exalted and high, mentioned, that He tests His creation, i.e., examines them with evil and good, He has explained in other places, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We tested them with good deeds and bad deeds, that they might return﴾ [al-A'raf: 168]

• And His saying: ﴿And We had certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, and We seized them with misfortune and hardship that they might humble themselves. So why did they not humble themselves when Our punishment came to them? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing. Then when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair. So the people who had wronged were eliminated. And praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 42–45]

• And His saying: ﴿And We did not send to any city a prophet except that We seized its people with adversity and hardship that they might supplicate [humbly]. Then We exchanged the bad state for good until they multiplied and said, "Adversity and ease have touched our forefathers." So We seized them suddenly while they were unaware﴾ [al-A'raf: 94–95]

and other verses besides these.

His saying, in these noble verses: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good﴾ indicates that "balā yablū" is used for testing with blessings and with calamities and afflictions. Some scholars said: most often "balā yablū" is used for evil, and "ablā yubli" for good. And the verse of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma combines both usages for good:

؎ May Allah reward with kindness what the two of them did for you, and tested them [with] the best of trials, which tests.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding His saying: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good﴾, that he said: i.e., We try you with evil and good as a trial: with hardship and ease, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, the lawful and the unlawful, obedience and disobedience, guidance and misguidance.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 36:

The Exalted says in this noble verse that when the disbelievers see the Prophet (ﷺ), they take him only as a mockery (﴿هُزُوًا﴾), meaning one who is ridiculed and belittled. The word *huzu'* (هُزُؤ) means derision, and it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) used as a description. They say: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, meaning: who disparages them, denies that they intercede for you or bring you near to God in nearness (﴿زُلْفَى﴾), and says that they neither benefit those who worship them nor harm those who do not worship them. Yet, despite all this, they are ﴿disbelievers in the Most Merciful﴾. The address in ﴿when he sees you﴾ is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and ﴿in﴾ in ﴿they take you﴾ is a negation particle.

Regarding the interrogative in ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, Abu Hayyan said in *al-Bahr* that it expresses denial and wonder. What appears to me is that by this interrogative they intend to belittle the Prophet (ﷺ), as indicated by the context of their saying ﴿they take you only as a mockery﴾. It is established in the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿani, the science of rhetorical meanings and purposes of speech) that among the purposes conveyed by the interrogative is belittlement.

Al-Qurtubi, in his interpretation of this verse, said that the answer to *idha* (إذا, "when") is the omitted verb of saying, and its implied form is: "When those who disbelieved see you, they say: Is this the one who mentions your gods?" He also said that the clause ﴿they take you only as a mockery﴾ is a parenthetical clause between *idha* and its answer. Abu Hayyan, in *al-Bahr*, preferred that the answer to *idha* is the clause ﴿they take you﴾, and said that the answer to *idha* introduced by the negating particles *in* or *ma* does not need to be joined with *fa'* (the particle of consequence).

As for ﴿mentions your gods﴾, it means disparages them. Among the uses of *dhikr* (mention) in the sense of disparagement is the Exalted's saying: ﴿They said: We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60], meaning: disparage them. And the saying of 'Antara:

*Do not mention my steed, or what I have fed it,*
*lest your skin become like the skin of a mangy camel.*

That is, do not disparage my steed. This was said by al-Qurtubi.

Al-Zamakhshari, in his interpretation of this noble verse, said: "Mention (*dhikr*) can be with good or with its opposite. When the circumstances indicate one of the two, it is used without qualification, as when you say to a man: 'I heard So-and-so mentioning you.' If the one mentioning is a friend, it is praise; if he is an enemy, it is blame. From this is the Exalted's saying: ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60], and His saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 36]." The end of the relevant point from him.

The clause in ﴿and they, in the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah). Some scholars said: the meaning of their disbelief in the mention of the Most Merciful is what is made clear in the Exalted's saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?" And it increases them in aversion﴾ [al-Furqan: 60]. And their saying: "We do not know the Most Merciful except the Most Merciful of Yamamah," meaning Musaylima the Liar.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others have explained that their denial of knowing the Most Merciful is ignorance feigned by them and obstinacy, although they know that "the Most Merciful" is among the names of God, the Exalted. He said: And one of the foolish poets of the Jahiliyyah said:

*Would that that girl had struck her she-camel,*
*would that my Lord, the Most Merciful, had cut off her right hand!*

And Salamah ibn Jandal al-Tuhawi said:

*You hastened against us with two hastenings of yours,*
*and whatever the Most Merciful wills, He binds and releases.*

In this noble verse there is clear evidence of the feebleness of the minds of the disbelievers, for they are devoted to mentioning idols that neither benefit nor harm, and it grieves them that these be mentioned with evil, or that it be said that they do not intercede and do not bring one near to God. As for the mention of God and what must be mentioned of Him, namely His oneness, they are disbelievers in it, not affirming it. They are more deserving that they be taken as a mockery by the Prophet (ﷺ), whom they took as a mockery, for he is in the right and they are in falsehood.

When you know the meaning of this noble verse, know that this meaning which it indicates is also made clear in surah al-Furqan, in the Exalted's saying: ﴿And when they see you, they take you only as a mockery: "Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger? He nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast toward them." And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan: 41–42]. So their belittling of him (ﷺ), cursed be they by God, which is mentioned in His saying in al-Anbiya', ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 36], is the same as that mentioned in al-Furqan: ﴿Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. And his mention of their gods with evil, mentioned in al-Anbiya' as ﴿mentions your gods﴾, is the same as that mentioned in al-Furqan in His saying: ﴿He nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast toward them﴾ [Ta-Ha: 42], meaning: because of what he makes clear of their defects, the uselessness of them, and the great harm of worshipping them.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 37:**

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not hasten Me.﴾

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that among the types of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars mention an opinion regarding a verse while the verse itself contains an indication (qarinah) pointing to the opposite of that opinion. Knowing this, be aware that in His words in this noble verse, ﴿of haste (ʿajal)﴾, there are two well-known opinions among the scholars, and within the verse itself there is an indication that one of them is not correct.

The opinion whose incorrectness is shown by the indication mentioned is the view of those who said that ʿajal means clay (ṭīn). This is a Himyarite dialect usage, as their poet said:

*Its growth is in the hard, barren rock,*
*and the palm grows between the water and the ʿajal.*

That is, between the water and the clay. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: "Man was created from clay,"

- like His words: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra: 61]
- and His words: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7]

The indication showing that ʿajal in the verse does not mean clay is His words that follow it: ﴿so do not hasten Me﴾.

- And His words: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 38]. This shows that the intended meaning of ʿajal is the haste that is the opposite of deliberation and steadiness.

The Arabs say, "He was created from such-and-such," meaning by this to emphasise the extent of the quality. For example, they say: "So-and-so was created from generosity (karam)," and "So-and-so woman was created from beauty (jamal)." Of this meaning is His saying: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness﴾ [al-Rum: 54], according to the more apparent view. This meaning is clarified by His words: ﴿And man invokes evil as he invokes good, and man has always been hasty﴾ [al-Isra: 11], that is, from his haste is his supplicating against himself or his child with evil.

Some scholars said: They used to seek hastily Allah's punishment and His signs that would compel them to knowledge and acknowledgement, saying, "When is this promise?" So He revealed His words: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ as a rebuke against that. It is as if He is saying to them: "It is not strange of you to be hasty, for you are created with this disposition; it is your nature and your temperament." Then He promised them that He would show them His signs, and forbade them to hasten, saying: ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not hasten Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 37], just as He said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Some people of knowledge said: The intended meaning of "man" in His words ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ is Adam. It is narrated from Said ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi: When the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise; when it entered his body he desired food, so he leapt up before the spirit reached his feet, hastening towards the fruits of Paradise. That is His saying: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾. It is also narrated from Mujahid, al-Kalbi and others: Adam was created on Friday at the end of the day, and when Allah brought his head to life, he hastened and sought the completion of the breathing of the spirit into him before the sun set.

Apparently these reports and similar ones are from the Israʾiliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin transmitted into Islamic exegesis). The most apparent view is that the meaning of the verse is that the nature of mankind is haste and lack of deliberation, as we have explained, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir said in his exegesis of this noble verse: The wisdom in mentioning human haste here is that when He mentioned those who mocked the Messenger (ﷺ), the desire for swift retribution against them arose in people's souls, and they hastened for it. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, because He the Exalted gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go. He postpones, then hastens; He gives time, then does not delay. For this reason He said: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾, that is, My vengeance, My judgement, and My power over those who disobeyed Me, so do not hasten. End of his words.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾

The answer to "law" (lawa, "if only") in this verse is omitted. We have already presented the evidence for this and its examples from the Arabic language in surah al-Baqarah (p. 151), and we pointed to it in surah Ibrahim and surah Yusuf. The meaning of the noble verse is: if only the disbelievers knew the time about which they ask, saying, "When is this promise?", a time that is difficult and severe, in which the Fire will surround them from behind and from in front. Then they will not be able to prevent it or repel it from themselves, nor will they find a helper to aid them, because of their being in that state of disbelief, mockery and hastening. But it is their ignorance of this that made it easy for them. What this noble verse contains of meanings has been explained in other places in the Book of Allah, exalted is He.

As for the Fire surrounding them on that day, it has been clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them from Hell will be a bed, and over them coverings.﴾ [al-A'raf: 41], to the end of the verse

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them there will be layers of Fire above them and layers below them. That is what Allah threatens His servants with. O My servants, fear Me.﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their garments will be of pitch, and the Fire will cover their faces.﴾ [Ibrahim: 50]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be grimacing.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 104], and other verses besides these. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Mighty, to protect us from it and from everything that brings us near to it, in word and deed. Indeed, He is near and responsive.

And what it contains of their being on that day, having no helper and no strength by which they can defend themselves, has been explained in other places.

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he will have no strength and no helper.﴾ [al-Tariq: 10]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they today are submitting.﴾ [al-Saffat: 25-26]

The verses on this are numerous.

What this verse points to, that what made that great day easy for them, so that they hastened it and mocked those who warned them of it, is only their ignorance of it, has also been explained in other places. As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and Allah will not fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾ [al-Hajj: 47] Also His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes to you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would be hastening?﴾ [Yunus: 50], and other verses besides these.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse, "If only they knew": some scholars said: the verb here is transitive, and the apparent reading is that it is cognitive (irfaniyyah), so it takes one object, as he indicated in the Khulasah with his saying:

"For knowledge of recognition and for suspicion (ẓann) and accusation, transitivity to one object is obligatory."

(p. 152) On this basis, the object here is His saying "ḥīna" (when), meaning: if only they recognised the time of the punishment befalling them and what it contains of horrors, they would not have treated it lightly or hastened it. On this basis, "ḥīn" is a direct object (maf'ul bihi), not an adverbial object (maf'ul fihi), because the knowledge which means recognition falls directly on the time mentioned. Some scholars said: the verb "to know" in this verse is treated as intransitive, so it does not fall on an object. On this reading the meaning is: if they had knowledge and were not ignorant, they would not have been hastening. On this basis the verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], meaning: he who has knowledge is not equal to he who has no knowledge. It has been established in the science of rhetoric (fann al-ma'ani) that when the purpose is to affirm the act of its doer in an affirmative statement, or to negate it from him in a negative statement, without regard to the act's connection to what it falls upon, it takes the status of an intransitive verb, as in His saying: ﴿Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], because what is intended is that the one who has the attribute of knowledge is not equal to the one who lacks it, and no consideration is given here to the knowledge falling on the things known by the one characterised by it. On this view, His saying ﴿when they will not be able to ward off﴾ is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, they will know that they were upon falsehood. The first reading is the more apparent. Abu Hayyan preferred the view that the object of "ya'lam" (knows) is omitted, and that it is what governs the adverbial phrase "ḥīna", and the estimated meaning is: if only those who disbelieved knew the coming of the promised thing they hastened, at the time when they will not be able to ward it off, they would not have disbelieved, hastened, or mocked.

Know that there is no difficulty in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ together with His saying: ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten﴾. It is not said: how can He say that man was created from haste and made disposed to it, and then forbid him from what he was created from and disposed to? That would be a charge of the impossible! We say: Yes, he was disposed to haste, but it is within his ability to bind himself to patience, just as he was disposed to love of desires, yet it is within his ability to restrain himself from them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be the refuge.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40-41]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 41:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but those who ridiculed them were enveloped by that which they used to mock.﴾

In this noble verse there is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, that his noble brothers among the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, were mocked by the disbelievers just as they mocked him ﷺ. That is: be patient as they were patient, and for you is the praiseworthy end and the ultimate victory, as it was for them. What this noble verse includes of this has come explained in several places in the Book of Allah.

Such as His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ [Fussilat: 43].

And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that which We strengthen your heart with﴾ [Hud: 120].

And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed until Our victory reached them. And none can alter the words of Allah. And there has already come to you some information about the messengers﴾ [Al-An'am: 34 — as numbered in the source: 6].

And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, then bear in mind that messengers before you were denied. To Allah will be returned all matters﴾ [Fatir: 4]. And His statement: ﴿And if they deny you, then those before them denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with scriptures and with the illuminating Book.﴾ ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My rejection?﴾ [Fatir: 25–26].

The verses of this kind are many.

As for His statement in this noble verse: ﴿So there enveloped those who ridiculed them﴾, meaning: it surrounded them. The root حاق (ḥāqa) is of the yāʾī ʿayn type (middle radical yāʾ), as evidenced by His statement in the present tense: ﴿And the evil plot does not envelop except its people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. This root is not used except for the enveloping of something disliked specifically. So you do not say: حاقَ بِهِ الخَيْرُ (ḥāqa bihi al-khayr, "good enveloped him") in the sense of surrounded him. The more apparent meaning of the verse is that what is intended is: and there enveloped them the punishment which they used to deny in the world and mock, and on this Ibn Kathir confined himself. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: ﴿So there enveloped﴾ meaning: surrounded and encircled those who disbelieved, and ridiculed them and mocked them (﴿what they used to mock﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 41]), meaning the recompense of their mocking. The first is more apparent, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted. The verse indicates that السُّخْرِيَة (sukhriyya, ridicule) is a form of الِاسْتِهْزاء (istihza', mockery), and this is well known.

The Lord, glorified and exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ in this noble verse to say to those who turn away from the remembrance of their Lord: ﴿Who is it that protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾ That is, who is it that guards and watches over you by night while you sleep, and by day while you go about your affairs? Al-kilāʾah (protection, guarding) with a kasra on the initial letter means safeguarding and watching over. It is said: "Go in the protection of Allah," meaning in His safekeeping. And "iktalaʾtu minhum" means "I guarded myself against them." From this is the verse of Ibn Harmah:

"Indeed Sulaymā, and Allah guards her, has held back from something that would not harm her."

And the verse of Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr:

"I made my camel kneel and kept watch over it with my eye, and I urged my soul: 'What shall I do?'"

As for "min" in His words "min al-Raḥmān," scholars have two well-known views concerning it. The first, on which Ibn Kathīr relied exclusively, is that "min" here means "instead of" (badal). On this view, "min al-Raḥmān" means "instead of the Most Merciful," that is, other than Him. Ibn Kathīr cited for this the verse of the rajaz poet:

"A young woman who has not worn the sheer silk, and has not tasted pistachio instead of vegetables."

That is, she has not tasted pistachio instead of vegetables. According to this view, the verse is like His words: ﴿Are you content with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], meaning instead of it. A parallel in the speech of the Arabs is the verse of the poet:

"They took the young she-camel (makhāḍ) from the weaned colt by force, unjustly, and it is recorded as a camel for the commander."

He means: they took, in zakāh, a makhāḍ instead of a faṣīl (weaned colt). The second view is that the meaning is ﴿who protects you﴾, that is, guards you ﴿from the Most Merciful﴾, that is, from His punishment and might. This is the more apparent view in my opinion. A Qur'anic parallel to it is His words: ﴿Who would help me against Allah if I disobeyed Him?﴾ [Hūd: 63], meaning: who would help me against Him, so as to repel His punishment from me.

Regarding the interrogative in His words "man yakla'ukum," Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr that it is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach. In my view it may carry the sense of denial (inkār) or of affirmation (taqrīr). Its denial sense is that the meaning is: there is no one at all who protects you from the punishment of Allah except Allah, the Exalted; so how can you worship other than Him? Its affirmative sense is that when they are asked, "Who protects you?", they are compelled to acknowledge that the one who protects them is Allah, because they know that none benefits or harms except Him, the Exalted. That is why they sincerely direct their supplication to Him in times of hardship and distress, and do not call upon anything alongside Him, as we have already mentioned, with the verses clarifying this in Surat al-Isrā' and elsewhere. When they acknowledge this, reproach and rebuke are directed at them: how can they divert the rights of the One who guards them by night and day to that which neither benefits nor harms?

This meaning which this noble verse points to, namely that no one can shield anyone from the punishment of Allah, and no one can protect or guard him from Allah, and that the true Guardian of everything is Allah alone, has been made clear in other places, such as:

• His words: ﴿For him there are successive angels before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Raʿd: 11], according to the most apparent interpretations;

• His words: ﴿Say: "Who can prevent anything from Allah for you if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you?"﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 11], and the verse continues;

• His words: ﴿Say: "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends evil for you or intends mercy for you?" They will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 17];

• His words: ﴿Say: "Who could prevent anything from Allah if He intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth entirely?"﴾ [al-Māʾidah: 17]

• His words: ﴿And He gives protection, and none can be protected against Him, if you should know﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 88];

besides other verses.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 21, verse 43:

His saying (may He be exalted): ﴿Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They are unable to help themselves, nor can they be companioned from Us.﴾

His saying in this noble verse: "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah), meaning "bal" (rather) and the hamzah (interrogative), so it includes the sense of turning away (idrab) and denial (inkar). The meaning is: Do they have gods that make them secure and mighty, so that Our punishment does not reach them? Then He clarified that their gods, which they claim, cannot benefit themselves, so how could they benefit others, by His saying: ﴿They are unable to help themselves﴾ [al-Anbiya': 43].

As for His saying "min duninā" (from besides Us), it has two possible readings. The first is that it is connected to "ālihah" (gods), meaning: Do they have gods besides Us (i.e., other than Us) that protect them from what We want to do to them of punishment? No, the matter is not so. The second is that it is connected to "tamna'uhum" (protect them), based on the saying of the Arabs: "manaʿtu dūnahu," meaning: I warded off harm from him. In my view the first is more apparent, and similar usages are numerous in the Qur'an,

such as His saying: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 29] etc.

And His saying: ﴿And they take besides Him gods﴾ [al-Furqan: 3] etc.

And what this noble verse includes, that the gods they have taken are unable to help themselves, so how could they help others, has come clarified in other places,

such as His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Do they associate with Him what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ ﴿And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves﴾ ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent﴾ ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you, so call upon them and let them respond to you, if you are truthful﴾ ﴿Do they have feet with which they walk, or hands with which they strike, or eyes with which they see, or ears with which they hear? Say: Call your associates, then conspire against me and give me no respite﴾ [al-A'raf: 191-195].

And His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves﴾ ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear, and you see them looking at you while they do not see﴾ [al-A'raf: 197].

And His saying (exalted is He): ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a speck﴾ ﴿If you call them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾ etc. [Fatir: 13-14].

And His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection﴾ etc. [al-Ahqaf: 5],

and other verses indicating that those deities worshipped besides Allah have no benefit whatsoever.

(p-156) As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Nor can they be companioned from Us﴾, meaning: they cannot be given protection (yujarun), i.e., those deities have no protector who shelters them from Us, because Allah grants protection and no one can be granted protection against Him, as He stated explicitly in the surah ﴿Certainly will the believers succeed﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88], in His saying: ﴿Say: In whose hand is the dominion of all things, and He grants protection while none can be protected against Him, if you know?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88]. The Arabs say: "I am a protector (jar) for you and a companion (sahib) against so-and-so," meaning: I am a protector for you from him. From this is the saying of the poet:

He calls out with the utmost of his voice, seeking refuge, so that he may be given protection from us while the spears are close upon him.

He means: so that he may be given protection and aid from us. Most of the scholars' statements on the verse return to what we have mentioned, such as the saying of some: "yuṣ'abūn" means "yumna'ūn" (they are prevented); and the saying of some: "yunṣarūn" (they are helped); and the saying of some: ﴿nor can they be companioned from Us﴾, meaning: Allah does not accompany them with good, and does not make mercy a companion to them. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 44:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until a long life passed over them﴾.

The apparent meaning is that the *idrab* (the transition from one statement to another) in "bal" ("nay," "rather") in this noble verse is *intiqali* (transitional). The demonstrative in His saying "these" refers back to those addressed earlier in His saying: ﴿Say: "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?"﴾, and so on. They are the disbelievers of Quraysh and whoever took gods besides Allah.

The meaning is that He gave these disbelievers and their fathers before them enjoyment through the bounties of worldly delights, so that their lifespans were prolonged in ease and blessing. This led them to transgression and obstinate persistence in disbelief.

What this noble verse includes, namely that Allah, may He be exalted, gives the disbelievers respite and lets them go on in blessing, and that this increases them in disbelief and misguidance, is clarified in many places in the Book of Allah, may He be exalted. Among them is His saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know. And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾ [al-A'raf: 182–183].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say: "Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You, but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance, and they were a people doomed to ruin"﴾ [al-Furqan: 18].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger. But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 29].

Verses of this kind are very many. And "al-'umr" (lifespan) is applied to the duration of life.
